profile.headline: Software Engineer - Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) Team at Okta, Inc.
profile.summary:
I am currently a Staff Software Engineer at Okta with over 7 years of experience specializing in backend development and customer-facing and enterprise software. I am comfortable working in all phases of the software development lifecycle and additionally have domain expertise in the identity & access management space. 

Feel free to contact me at kenton.smith22@gmail.com.

positions.title: Software Engineer - Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) Team
positions.description:
•	Created an internal test web application to help other engineers and QA test Okta's Factor API for the Fido U2F factor type.
•	Fixed complicated, cross-cutting bugs for numerous customers.  Each of these customers had a unique, complex environment in which they were integrating with Okta.  Worked closely with customer support while troubleshooting and also kept customers informed with progress updates.
•	Added support in the Okta Factors API for Fido U2F factor enrollment and verification.  https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/resources/factors
•	Made enhancements to the Okta Verify mobile app's Auto-Push feature.
•	I am currently an intern coordinator for the San Jose location in the summer of 2018.  I organize events/meetings for interns and communicate with each intern's mentor to make sure their experience at Okta is awesome!
•	Worked on Lifecycle Automation (LCA) team for first three months then was transferred to MFA team. Worked mostly on group rules enhancements while I was on the LCA team.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern - Identity Lifecycle Management Team
positions.description:
Project Overview: Create additional reporting capabilities for Okta IT admins so they are better able to handle auditing and compliance-related requests.  

Tasks Performed:
•	Created API endpoints for front-end to call that would create diff report job, fetch latest run diff report, get job meta data (things such as status so in-progress/completed), and directly export csv file.  
•	Worked and communicated closely with UI engineer, UX designer, Product Management Intern, and QA engineer during the course of the summer.
•	Consolidated application user assignment and deprovisioning details across several databases and tables.  This information can be leveraged for any future reports.  
•	Documented details of project (purpose, architecture, known issues, limitations).
•	Provided UI Engineer with thorough API spec to ensure things worked seamlessly end-to-end.     
•	Wrote unit and functional tests alongside any code changes to ensure new functionality worked and also for regression testing purposes.   
•	Conducted performance tests on job run times (reports were created in an asynchronous job).  
•	Presented project to the entire engineering team during the engineering intern fair.  

Technologies Used: Java, SQL, Hibernate, Spring, Git, JUnit, EasyMock, Confluence, and JIRA.  

Results:
•	Reporting features I developed were released to the Beta stage for Okta’s IT product for select customers to try.
•	Reporting features I developed were a part of the demo script for a keynote presentation at Oktane16, Okta’s annual identity-as-a-service conference.

positions.description:

positions.title: Software Development Engineering Intern

•	Documented all work for future reference and maintainability.

projects.title: Okta 2016 Engineering Intern Hackathon - Suspicious User Detection System
projects.description:
My specific contributions to group hackathon project:
•	Created backend endpoint that would leverage Okta’s system log micro-service and retrieve recently failed multi-factor authentication login events.
•	Extended Okta’s notification functionality so that end-users could notify their IT admin if a suspicious login was not actually him/her.  For example, based on the notification received, an IT admin could take action by blocking that particular IP address that was associated with the failed multi-factor authentication login attempt.

Outcome:  Out of four teams our group won first place for the hackathon.  Winners were decided by votes from all full-time engineers.     

Project Overview: The purpose of this hackathon was to add an enhancement to Okta's IT product or platform product.  There were four teams of interns, with four interns on each team.  We had 72 hours to turn an idea into a working demo and also create a presentation that would communicate the business value of our enhancement.  My group hackathon project was called "Suspicious User Detection System" or "SUDS".  The main idea idea of this hack was to give more power to Okta end-users to report failed multi-factor authentication (MFA) login attempts on their account.  When recently failed MFA events were detected, an informative modal would show up and display information about the failed event (IP address, location, date, time, etc.) as well as two options for user select.  The first option was essentially a button that would indicate that the enduser was actually the person who failed MFA.  The second option was a button that would indicate that the person who failed MFA was not the legitimate enduser, and would send a notification to the enduser's IT admin who could then investigate further.
